content: Clotrimazole (vaginal) is an antifungal medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of vulvar itching and irritation. Common side effects include nausea and vomiting. For adult patients, clotrimazole (vaginal) is indicated as a vaginal antifungal and external vulvar antifungal. There is limited information regarding off-label uses, whether guideline-supported or not, for adult patients. In pediatric patients, there is limited information regarding FDA-labeled indications or off-label uses of clotrimazole (vaginal), whether guideline-supported or not. Contraindications for clotrimazole (vaginal) are not well-documented in the drug label. However, warnings include the following: It is for vaginal or external vulvar use only. Do not use if you experience abdominal pain, fever, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge. Contact your doctor immediately. Do not use in children under 12 years of age without consulting a doctor. If you are experiencing vaginal or vulvar itching and discomfort for the first time, consult a doctor before use. If you have been previously diagnosed with a vaginal yeast infection and are experiencing the same symptoms, use the cream as directed for seven consecutive days. If symptoms return within two months or the infection does not resolve easily with proper treatment, consult a doctor. This could indicate pregnancy or an underlying medical condition such as diabetes or a compromised immune system (e.g., due to HIV infection). Do not use tampons while using this product. Stop use and consult a doctor if symptoms do not improve within three days or if the infection is not resolved within seven days. This may indicate a condition other than a yeast infection. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. Keep out of reach of children. If swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Adverse reactions reported post-marketing include nausea and vomiting. There is limited information regarding clinical trial experiences, drug interactions, and monitoring for clotrimazole (vaginal). Regarding use in specific populations: There is no FDA guidance on the use of clotrimazole (vaginal) during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or in nursing mothers. There is no FDA guidance on its use in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, or racial populations. There is no FDA guidance on its use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, or in immunocompromised patients. Clotrimazole (vaginal) is administered topically. There is limited information regarding its monitoring, IV compatibility, overdose, mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, nonclinical toxicology, and clinical studies in the drug label. Storage information and patient counseling details are also limited in the drug label. The interaction between alcohol and clotrimazole (vaginal) has not been established, so patients should consult their doctor regarding alcohol use while taking this medication. The brand name for clotrimazole (vaginal) is CLOTRIMAZOLE®. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names in the drug label.
